subject: Re: Competitive eval — model quality follow-up
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive eval follow-up — next tests and prompts

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

Summary of call:
- Goal: validate model quality differences (hallucination, instruction-following, LLM safety filters) across Redwood hosted models vs Hyperscaler A and Hyperscaler B endpoints for Acme's internal knowledge prompts.
- Success criteria: <=3% critical hallucinations, <5% instruction-failure on core tasks, comparable latency within 20% for typical 256-token responses.

Proposed immediate next tests (need your sign-off):
1) Run the 120-prompt eval set we demoed (attached prompt-set-v3.txt) against Redwood baseline (redwood-medium-v2) and Hyperscaler A/B standard endpoints.
2) Include explicit hallucination probe prompts and factual-regression checks — we will flag any hallucinations and capture "hallucination_type" in the CSV.
3) Produce a per-prompt CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, model, raw_response, hallucination_flag, hallucination_notes, latency_ms, tokens_out. (sample schema attached)
4) For any regression >5% on instruction-following compared to hyperscaler baseline, we propose a short fine-tune / prompt-tuning experiment and will share cost/time estimates.

Attachments: prompt-set-v3.txt (prompt set), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-onepager.pdf (one-pager on differentiators).

Can you confirm we have permission to send test data (anonymized snippets) to Hyperscaler endpoints and to share the CSV back to your security team if they request it? If yes, we'll schedule the run for Wednesday and share interim raw results by Friday.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@acmecorp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: John Patel <john.patel@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive eval follow-up — next tests and prompts

Rachel — thanks for the clear recap. Confirmed: please proceed with the evals. A few clarifications from our side:

- Data & security: you may send anonymized prompt snippets to the hyperscaler endpoints; do not include any PII. Our security team (cc'd) requests that the returned CSV is uploaded to our secure SharePoint link (I included John who owns that).
- Hallucination checks: please include both binary hallucination_flag and a short free-text note when it's a critical hallucination (i.e., inventing a nonexistent policy or fabricating a quote). We will use that for our remediation conversation.
- Format: CSV as you described is fine. Please also include a quick summary sheet with aggregated metrics (hallucination rate, avg latency, instruction-fail rate) per model.

If you can run the tests on Wed as proposed and share interim results by Friday EOD PST, we'll review with engineering and aim to have feedback by next Tuesday.

Appreciate the responsiveness — Alex
Alex Jenkins
CIO, Acme Corp
alex.jenkins@acmecorp.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive eval follow-up — test plan & run schedule

Team — per Rachel/Alex, planning to run the full 120-prompt set Wednesday (2027-03-31) and return an interim CSV by Friday 2027-04-02 EOD PST. Proposed execution notes: 

Execution plan:
- Redwood baseline: redwood-medium-v2 (quantized fp16 path). Run 3 seeds to capture variance; capture avg latency and 90th percentile.
- Hyperscaler A/B: standard gen endpoints (we'll use their 'balanced' and 'accurate' profiles).
- Metrics captured: hallucination_flag (binary), hallucination_severity (minor/major/critical), instruction_follow (pass/fail), avg_token_prob (where available), latency_ms, tokens_out.
- Regression checks: we'll compute model delta vs Hyperscaler A (baseline) and flag any prompt where redwood delta in instruction_fail_rate >5% or hallucination_rate increases >3%.

Attachments: acme-eval-results.csv (template), prompt-set-v3.txt (confirmed). I also attached the one-pager PDF to summarize differentiators for Alex.

Notes on differentiators to highlight in the summary:
- Prefix/KV caching improved our effective latency on repeated-context prompts — include a small A/B showing cached vs cold responses.
- Token-level cost vs Hyperscaler B (preliminary looks ~18% lower for equivalent quality on these prompt classes).

Rachel — tagging you for any additional requirements from Acme before we kick off.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@acmecorp.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive eval — interim results + next steps

Alex — we completed the first pass of the run and uploaded the interim CSV to your Drive link (https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-evals). Key highlights from the 120-prompt set (interim):

Top-level aggregated metrics (Redwood vs Hyperscaler A/B):
- Hallucination rate (critical): Redwood 2.1% | Hyperscaler A 3.4% | Hyperscaler B 2.7%
- Instruction-fail rate: Redwood 4.6% | Hyperscaler A 3.9% | Hyperscaler B 5.2%
- Avg latency (256-token estimate): Redwood 320ms | Hyperscaler A 280ms | Hyperscaler B 410ms
- Avg tokens_out: comparable across models (~210 tokens)

Initial interpretation:
- Redwood meets your critical hallucination target (<3%) and is better than Hyperscaler A in this run. Instruction-following is within ~0.7% of Hyperscaler A but slightly worse — this is in line with the expected behavior for more conservative decoding defaults.
- Where instruction-fail regressions exceed 5% (12 prompts flagged), Marissa suggests a prompt-tuning pass which we estimate at ~4 hours of compute and ~$450 in run cost for a ~2-3% improvement. We can run a focused prompt-tune on the flagged prompt subset if you want faster turnaround.

Next steps proposed:
1) Review interim CSV and the per-prompt notes (there are 12 flagged instruction regressions and 5 critical hallucinations).
2) If you want, we'll run targeted prompt-tuning on the flagged subset and re-run metrics within 48 hours.
3) Attend a short 30-min walkthrough Wed 2027-04-06 to review examples, logs, and recommended config changes (we'll send calendar invite).

Attachments: acme-eval-results.csv (interim, uploaded).

Alex — let me know whether to proceed with targeted prompt-tuning. If helpful, we can also run the same 120 prompts against a quantized redwood-large-v1 to evaluate headroom; that will add ~6 hours to runs and an estimate in the summary.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Product, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
